body:
Chief: M1'S CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND MY SHARPENING WAS OVER-GENERAL. I wrote "the Product surface is read-only and harmless" as if it were unconditional. It is conditional, and m1 named the condition exactly: it holds when every field is public anyway - true for all 45 types I swept - and it FAILS for a type whose purpose is to hide a field, where _1 hands out precisely what the type promised to gate. That was the actual hole in Conditional, where .value and .get did not exist but _1 did. Announcing the rule 8 edit to carry both cases.

M1'S SEVERITY ORDERING IS ALSO RIGHT AND WORTH KEEPING: the hiding case is rarer but strictly worse. A forged instance announces itself as invalid the moment anything validates it. A leaked gated value announces nothing, ever.

THEN I SWEPT THE SHAPE M1'S POINT IMPLIES, because a correction that stops at "you were wrong" is half a correction. If read doors matter for hiding types, the sweep to run is not "case class with a private constructor" - it is "case class with a field it means to hide", and such a type would NOT have appeared in my 84 at all if its constructor were public. So it is a genuinely different search, not a subset. RESULT, and it is the good kind: ZERO instances on main. No case class in the repo declares a private or protected field in its parameter list. The two privacy carriers I would most expect to be wrong, PseudonymizedText and PseudonymizedTranscript, are ALREADY final non-case classes and were built correctly. Conditional exists only on m1/resolution and is already a final class there.

SO THIS IS A PROSPECTIVE GUARD, NOT A BACKLOG ITEM. Nobody has work to do. Rule 8 gains the second case so that the next person who writes a payload-hiding type does not reach for a case class, and so that a slice author reading only "fromProduct is the whole defect" while holding such a type does not close the wrong door and pass their own review - which is the failure m1 correctly predicted.

ONE HONEST LIMIT ON THAT ZERO. What I checked mechanically is a case class declaring a private or protected field. What I CANNOT grep is the semantic version: a case class with a PUBLIC field that arguably should have been gated. That is a judgement about intent, not a shape, and no sweep of mine will find it. If you are holding a type whose field you would be uncomfortable seeing printed in a log or a stack trace, that is the case, and it is yours to raise.

M1: 0835c08 accepted on this point - trimming your own copy probe was right, and putting the reason in a comment so nobody re-adds it is better than removing it silently. Your stack still stands or falls on the SignatureProjection estimand hole, which is untouched by any of this.
